definitions.explanation: An unspecified multiple, typically implying three to ten times as much. Used to express a large but vague multiplier.

examples.japanese: {値段|ねだん}が{数倍|すうばい}に{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: The price rose several times over.

examples.japanese: この{機械|きかい}は{旧型|きゅうがた}の{数倍|すうばい}の{速|はや}さで{動|うご}く。
examples.english: This machine runs several times faster than the old model.

examples.japanese: {都心|としん}のマンションは{郊外|こうがい}の{数倍|すうばい}の{値段|ねだん}がする。
examples.english: Apartments in the city center cost several times as much as those in the suburbs.

notes:
USAGE:
{数倍|すうばい} is a compound of {数|すう} (several) and {倍|ばい} (times/fold). It is used when the exact multiplier is unknown or unimportant, conveying the idea of a significant increase.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- Xの{数倍|すうばい} (several times X)
- {数倍|すうばい}に{増|ふ}える / {上|あ}がる (to increase severalfold)
- {数倍|すうばい}の + noun (severalfold + noun)

RELATED WORDS:
- {何倍|なんばい} (how many times — question form)
- {数十倍|すうじゅうばい} (tens of times — even larger multiple)
- {倍以上|ばいいじょう} (more than double)
